name: bird-04-reactor-geometry
question:
Can the reactor support a stirred-tank kLa correlation (the benchmark
geometry) alongside the bubble-column form, selectable by configuration?
hypothesis:
A geometry configuration field selects the kLa correlation, and under
stirred-tank geometry kLa matches the published correlation for the
configured power input and superficial gas velocity within tolerance.
objective:
Add a selectable stirred-tank kLa correlation and measure kLa against the
published correlation to determine the model can be parameterized to a
specific vessel.
description:
The high-cell-density benchmark uses a stirred-tank vessel; the current
transport form assumes bubble-column. This study adds a configurable
geometry and validates the stirred-tank kLa against literature, resolving
the reactor-geometry-for-benchmark question from mbp-03. Builds on the
coupled loop established in bird-02.

expected_behavior.name: geometry-selectable-via-config
expected_behavior.en: Reactor geometry (stirred-tank vs bubble-column) is chosen by a configuration field, selecting the active kLa correlation.
expected_behavior.notes: Verified by tests/test_bird04_geometry.py::test_geometry_selectable_via_config — reactor_type selects the gas-holdup correlation, and the kla_correlation default 'auto' resolves the kLa form from geometry (vant_riet for stirred_tank, higbie otherwise); 'higbie'|'vant_riet' force a specific form independent of geometry.

expected_behavior.name: kla-matches-stirred-tank-correlation
expected_behavior.en: Under stirred-tank geometry, computed kLa matches the published correlation for the configured power input and superficial gas velocity within tolerance.
expected_behavior.notes: Verified by tests/test_bird04_geometry.py::test_kla_matches_stirred_tank_correlation — computed kLa equals the published Van't Riet (1979) coalescing-media form 0.026·(P/V)^0.4·u_g^0.5 at the configured P/V and u_g (see literature_anchors).

literature_anchors.expectation: Stirred-tank kLa follows Van't Riet (1979): kLa[1/s] = 0.026·(P/V)^0.4·u_g^0.5 for coalescing media (water).
literature_anchors.source: Van't Riet 1979, Ind. Eng. Chem. Process Des. Dev. 18(3):357-364
